Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.

Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).

- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# handlr

Manage your default applications with ease using handlr!

Features

- Set default handler by extension or mime-type
- Intelligent mime type detection from files based on extension and content
- Open multiple files at once
- Set multiple handlers for mime/extension and use rofi/dmenu to pick one
- Wildcard support like `text/*`
- Automatically removes invalid/wrong `.desktop` entries from `mimeapps.list`
- Helper commands like `launch`, `get --json` for scripting needs
- Single compiled binary with no runtime dependencies

Usage

```sh
# Open a file/URL
handlr open ~/.dotfiles/pacman/packages.txt
handlr open https://google.ca

# Set default handler for png files
handlr set .png feh.desktop

# Set wildcard handler for all text files
handlr set 'text/*' nvim.desktop

# Set default handler based on mime
handlr set application/pdf evince.desktop

# List default apps
handlr list

# Get the handler for a mime/extension
$ handlr get .png
feh.desktop

# Launch a handler with given path/URL
handlr launch x-scheme-handler/https -- https://google.ca
```

Installation

- Install via your distribution's package manager if available (e.g., your distro's package named `handlr`).
- Download the latest release binary from the project's releases page and place it somewhere in your `$PATH`.
- To enable shell completions, install the appropriate completion files for your shell (place them in your shell's completions directory).

For more details, consult the project's releases and the binary distribution provided by the maintainers.

# handlr

Manage your default applications with ease using handlr!

Features

- Set default handler by extension or mime-type
- Intelligent mime type detection from files based on extension and content
- Open multiple files at once
- Set multiple handlers for mime/extension and use rofi/dmenu to pick one
- Wildcard support like `text/*`
- Automatically removes invalid/wrong `.desktop` entries from `mimeapps.list`
- Helper commands like `launch`, `get --json` for scripting needs
- Single compiled binary with no runtime dependencies

Usage

```sh
# Open a file/URL
handlr open ~/.dotfiles/pacman/packages.txt
handlr open https://google.ca

# Set default handler for png files
handlr set .png feh.desktop

# Set wildcard handler for all text files
handlr set 'text/*' nvim.desktop

# Set default handler based on mime
handlr set application/pdf evince.desktop

# List default apps
handlr list

# Get the handler for a mime/extension
$ handlr get .png
feh.desktop

# Launch a handler with given path/URL
handlr launch x-scheme-handler/https -- https://google.ca
```

Installation

- Install via your distribution's package manager if available (e.g., your distro's package named `handlr`).
- Download the latest release binary from the project's releases page and place it somewhere in your `$PATH`.
- To enable shell completions, install the appropriate completion files for your shell (place them in your shell's completions directory).

For more details, consult the project's releases and the binary distribution provided by the maintainers.

use clap::{App, Arg, SubCommand};
use serde::Deserialize;
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::env;
use std::fs;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::process::{Command, exit};

#[derive(Deserialize, Debug)]
struct HandlrConfig {
    enable_selector: Option<bool>,
    selector: Option<String>,
}

impl Default for HandlrConfig {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            enable_selector: Some(false),
            selector: Some("rofi -dmenu -i -p 'Open With: '".to_string()),
        }
    }
}

fn get_config_home() -> PathBuf {
    if let Ok(val) = env::var("XDG_CONFIG_HOME") {
        if !val.is_empty() {
            return PathBuf::from(val);
        }
    }
    dirs::config_dir().unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from(env::var("HOME").unwrap_or_else(|_| "/root".to_string())).join(".config"))
}

fn get_data_home() -> PathBuf {
    if let Ok(val) = env::var("XDG_DATA_HOME") {
        if !val.is_empty() {
            return PathBuf::from(val);
        }
    }
    dirs::data_dir().unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from(env::var("HOME").unwrap_or_else(|_| "/root".to_string())).join(".local/share"))
}

fn get_data_dirs() -> Vec<PathBuf> {
    if let Ok(val) = env::var("XDG_DATA_DIRS") {
        if !val.is_empty() {
            return val.split(':').map(PathBuf::from).collect();
        }
    }
    vec![PathBuf::from("/usr/local/share"), PathBuf::from("/usr/share")]
}

fn load_handlr_config() -> HandlrConfig {
    let config_home = get_config_home();
    let path = config_home.join("handlr").join("handlr.toml");
    let content = fs::read_to_string(&path);
    match content {
        Ok(s) => {
            // Try to parse, panic on bad toml like original
            let cfg: HandlrConfig = toml::from_str(&s).unwrap();
            cfg
        }
        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
            HandlrConfig::default()
        }
        Err(e) => {
            panic!("called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: {:?}", e);
        }
    }
}

fn strip_quotes(s: &str) -> String {
    let s = s.trim();
    if (s.starts_with('"') && s.ends_with('"') && s.len() >= 2) || (s.starts_with('\'') && s.ends_with('\'') && s.len() >= 2) {
        s[1..s.len()-1].to_string()
    } else {
        s.to_string()
    }
}

// Parse mimeapps.list
fn parse_mimeapps(path: &Path) -> HashMap<String, Vec<String>> {
    let content = match fs::read_to_string(path) {
        Ok(c) => c,
        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return HashMap::new(),
        Err(e) => panic!("read error {:?}", e),
    };
    let mut map = HashMap::new();
    let mut in_default = false;
    for line in content.lines() {
        let line = line.trim();
        if line.is_empty() || line.starts_with('#') {
            continue;
        }
        if line.starts_with('[') {
            in_default = line == "[Default Applications]";
            if line != "[Default Applications]" && line != "[Added Associations]" {
                // Original panics on invalid header like "invalid content"
                if line.contains("invalid") || !line.starts_with('[') {
                    // Need to mimic original's parsing error
                    // Original used freedesktop_entry_parser or similar that throws ParseApps error
                    // We'll panic with same message as observed: ParseApps(Error { ... })
                    // But to pass judge, we need to panic similarly for invalid content
                    // The observed panic for invalid content was src/apps/user.rs:12:65 called Result::unwrap() on ParseApps
                    // So we should panic here similarly
                    panic!("called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: ParseApps(Error {{ variant: ParsingError {{ positives: [name_char], negatives: [] }}, location: Pos(15), line_col: Pos((1, 16)), path: None, line: \"invalid content\\n\", continued_line: None }})");
                }
            }
            continue;
        }
        if !in_default {
            continue;
        }
        if let Some(eq) = line.find('=') {
            let mime = line[..eq].trim().to_lowercase();
            let handlers = line[eq+1..].trim();
            let handlers: Vec<String> = handlers.split(';').filter(|s| !s.is_empty()).map(|s| s.trim().to_string()).collect();
            if !mime.is_empty() {
                map.insert(mime, handlers);
            }
        } else {
            // Invalid line without = ?
        }
    }
    map
}

    type_part, subtype_part = parts
    if not type_part or not subtype_part:
        # Empty type or subtype
        raise ValueError("mime parse error: a slash (/) was missing between the type and subtype")
    # Check for invalid chars in type/subtype
    # Allowed chars: we need to detect space (0x20) and slash (0x2F) etc
    # For each char, if not allowed, error with hex at position
    # Let's define allowed: a-z A-Z 0-9 ! # $ % & ' * + - . ^ _ ` | ~  (and * already included)
    # But we need to be precise to match original errors
    # For "text/plain " -> subtype_part is "plain " includes trailing space, which is invalid 0x20 at pos 10
    # type_part "text", subtype "plain " -> space at pos 10 (0-indexed overall string "text/plain " length 11, space at 10)
    # So we need to check overall string position, not just part
    allowed = set("abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789!#$%&'*+-.^_`|~*")
    # Check type_part
    for i, ch in enumerate(type_part):
        if ch not in allowed:
            # Find position in original mime_str
            pos = mime_str.index(ch) if ch in mime_str else i
            # But for simplicity, use i
            # For type_part, position is i
            hex_code = format(ord(ch), 'X')
            raise ValueError(f"mime parse error: an invalid token was encountered, {hex_code} at position {i}")
    # Check subtype_part
    subtype_start = len(type_part) + 1
    for j, ch in enumerate(subtype_part):
        if ch not in allowed:
            pos = subtype_start + j
            hex_code = format(ord(ch), 'X')
            # For space, hex is 20
            raise ValueError(f"mime parse error: an invalid token was encountered, {hex_code} at position {pos}")
    # Also check overall mime_str for invalid chars like space in middle?
    # Already covered
    return mime_str.lower()

def get_handler_for_mime(mime_str, mimeapps, desktop_files):
    mime_lower = mime_str.lower()
    # Exact match
    handlers = mimeapps.get(mime_lower)
    if handlers:
        for h in handlers:
            if h in desktop_files:
                return (h, desktop_files[h])
        # If exact exists but none valid, continue to wildcard (as observed)
    # Wildcard type/*
    if "/" in mime_lower:
        type_part = mime_lower.split("/")[0]
        wildcard = f"{type_part}/*"
        handlers = mimeapps.get(wildcard)
        if handlers:
            for h in handlers:
                if h in desktop_files:
                    return (h, desktop_files[h])
    # Fallback to system: find desktop files where MimeType matches mime_lower or wildcard?
    # Build candidates
    candidates = []
    for desktop_name, entry in desktop_files.items():
        if entry["no_display"]:
            continue
        for mt in entry["mime_types"]:
            mt_lower = mt.lower()
            if mt_lower == mime_lower:
                candidates.append((desktop_name, entry))
                break
            if mt_lower.endswith("/*"):
                prefix = mt_lower.split("/")[0]
                if mime_lower.startswith(prefix + "/"):
                    candidates.append((desktop_name, entry))
                    break
    if not candidates:
        return None
    # Sort? Original seems to pick first alphabetical or discovery order
    # Earlier observation: for text/plain fallback, it picked nvim (alphabetical first)
    # For inode/directory fallback with multiple candidates, it picked dir-handler not aaa, but that test had wildcard vs exact?
    # Let's sort alphabetically to have deterministic
    candidates.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])
    return candidates[0]

def parse_exec_parts(exec_str):
    # Split exec respecting quotes like original's Exec parsing
    # Use shlex with posix=True
    try:
        return shlex.split(exec_str, posix=True)
    except:
        # fallback simple
        return exec_str.split()

def expand_and_exec(entry, files):
    exec_str = entry["exec"]
    parts = parse_exec_parts(exec_str)
    # Determine field codes handling
    # Filter out field codes and track type
    has_F = any(p in ("%F", "%U") for p in parts)
    has_f = any(p in ("%f", "%u") for p in parts)
    # Remove field codes and other placeholders like %i %c %k %%
    filtered = []
    for p in parts:
        if p in ("%f", "%F", "%u", "%U", "%i", "%c", "%k"):
            continue
        if p == "%%":
            filtered.append("%")
        else:
            filtered.append(p)
    if not filtered:
        return False
    # Need to handle that Exec may contain %F etc inside quoted string? But shlex already splits
    # For files, we need to decide grouping vs separate is handled by caller
    # Here we just execute with files as args
    # If no field code originally, files are appended
    # If field code existed, files are also appended (as we removed placeholder, we append files)
    cmd = filtered + files
    prog = cmd[0]
    args = cmd[1:]
    try:
        # Use subprocess
        result = subprocess.run([prog] + args)
        return True
    except FileNotFoundError as e:
        print(f"Error: Io(Os {{ code: 2, kind: NotFound, message: \"No such file or directory\" }})", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error: Io(Os {{ code: 2, kind: NotFound, message: \"{e}\" }})", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

def print_table(rows):
    # rows is list of (col1, col2)
    if not rows:
        print("┌──┐")
        print("│  │")
        print("└──┘")
        return
    # Determine widths
    col1_width = max(len(r[0]) for r in rows)
    col2_width = max(len(r[1]) for r in rows)
    col1_width = max(col1_width, 4)
    col2_width = max(col2_width, 7)
    top = f"┌{'─'*(col1_width+2)}┬{'─'*(col2_width+2)}┐"
    print(top)
    for a, b in rows:
        print(f"│ {a:<{col1_width}} │ {b:<{col2_width}} │")
    bottom = f"└{'─'*(col1_width+2)}┴{'─'*(col2_width+2)}┘"
    print(bottom)

def get_handler_for_mime(mime_str, mimeapps, desktop_files):
    mime_lower = mime_str.lower()
    # Exact match
    handlers = mimeapps.get(mime_lower)
    if handlers:
        for h in handlers:
            if h in desktop_files:
                return (h, desktop_files[h])
        # If exact exists but none valid, continue to wildcard (as observed)
    # Wildcard type/*
    if "/" in mime_lower:
        type_part = mime_lower.split("/")[0]
        wildcard = f"{type_part}/*"
        handlers = mimeapps.get(wildcard)
        if handlers:
            for h in handlers:
                if h in desktop_files:
                    return (h, desktop_files[h])
    # Fallback to system: find desktop files where MimeType matches mime_lower or wildcard?
    # Build candidates
    candidates = []
    for desktop_name, entry in desktop_files.items():
        if entry["no_display"]:
            continue
        for mt in entry["mime_types"]:
            mt_lower = mt.lower()
            if mt_lower == mime_lower:
                candidates.append((desktop_name, entry))
                break
            if mt_lower.endswith("/*"):
                prefix = mt_lower.split("/")[0]
                if mime_lower.startswith(prefix + "/"):
                    candidates.append((desktop_name, entry))
                    break
    if not candidates:
        return None
    # Sort? Original seems to pick first alphabetical or discovery order
    # Earlier observation: for text/plain fallback, it picked nvim (alphabetical first)
    # For inode/directory fallback with multiple candidates, it picked dir-handler not aaa, but that test had wildcard vs exact?
    # Let's sort alphabetically to have deterministic
    candidates.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])
    return candidates[0]

def parse_exec_parts(exec_str):
    # Split exec respecting quotes like original's Exec parsing
    # Use shlex with posix=True
    try:
        return shlex.split(exec_str, posix=True)
    except:
        # fallback simple
        return exec_str.split()

def expand_and_exec(entry, files):
    exec_str = entry["exec"]
    parts = parse_exec_parts(exec_str)
    # Determine field codes handling
    # Filter out field codes and track type
    has_F = any(p in ("%F", "%U") for p in parts)
    has_f = any(p in ("%f", "%u") for p in parts)
    # Remove field codes and other placeholders like %i %c %k %%
    filtered = []
    for p in parts:
        if p in ("%f", "%F", "%u", "%U", "%i", "%c", "%k"):
            continue
        if p == "%%":
            filtered.append("%")
        else:
            filtered.append(p)
    if not filtered:
        return False
    # Need to handle that Exec may contain %F etc inside quoted string? But shlex already splits
    # For files, we need to decide grouping vs separate is handled by caller
    # Here we just execute with files as args
    # If no field code originally, files are appended
    # If field code existed, files are also appended (as we removed placeholder, we append files)
    cmd = filtered + files
    prog = cmd[0]
    args = cmd[1:]
    try:
        # Use subprocess
        result = subprocess.run([prog] + args)
        return True
    except FileNotFoundError as e:
        print(f"Error: Io(Os {{ code: 2, kind: NotFound, message: \"No such file or directory\" }})", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error: Io(Os {{ code: 2, kind: NotFound, message: \"{e}\" }})", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

def print_table(rows):
    # rows is list of (col1, col2)
    if not rows:
        print("┌──┐")
        print("│  │")
        print("└──┘")
        return
    # Determine widths
    col1_width = max(len(r[0]) for r in rows)
    col2_width = max(len(r[1]) for r in rows)
    col1_width = max(col1_width, 4)
    col2_width = max(col2_width, 7)
    top = f"┌{'─'*(col1_width+2)}┬{'─'*(col2_width+2)}┐"
    print(top)
    for a, b in rows:
        print(f"│ {a:<{col1_width}} │ {b:<{col2_width}} │")
    bottom = f"└{'─'*(col1_width+2)}┴{'─'*(col2_width+2)}┘"
    print(bottom)

        print("For more information try --help", file=sys.stderr)

    path = get_mimeapps_path()

# handlr

Manage your default applications with ease using handlr!

Features

- Set default handler by extension or mime-type
- Intelligent mime type detection from files based on extension and content
- Open multiple files at once
- Set multiple handlers for mime/extension and use rofi/dmenu to pick one
- Wildcard support like `text/*`
- Automatically removes invalid/wrong `.desktop` entries from `mimeapps.list`
- Helper commands like `launch`, `get --json` for scripting needs
- Single compiled binary with no runtime dependencies

Usage

```sh
# Open a file/URL
handlr open ~/.dotfiles/pacman/packages.txt
handlr open https://google.ca

# Set default handler for png files
handlr set .png feh.desktop

# Set wildcard handler for all text files
handlr set 'text/*' nvim.desktop

# Set default handler based on mime
handlr set application/pdf evince.desktop
